stops.whatYouCanSeeToday: Surrounded by whispering Tuscan fir forests overlooking Florence’s distant terracotta domes, **Monte Senario Sanctuary** still welcomes weary travelers—and the Servite friars still craft their famous herbal *Gemma d’Abeto* mountain elixir!

hiddenArtifacts.storyUnlocked: How did the universal Feast of **Our Lady of Sorrows** spread across Europe? Meditating daily on Mary’s brave, tearful fidelity beneath the Cross (*"Stabat Mater"* — "The Mother stood!"), the Servites popularized devotion to Our Lady of Sorrows as a beacon of compassion and peacemaking across the world!

stops.subtitle: Sweep your lantern across Pietà of Michelangelo, St. Peter’s Basilica to uncover 3 hidden memories
stops.eraLabel: 1499 – Present · St. Peter’s Basilica, Vatican City
stops.ancientPlaceName: Pietà of Michelangelo, St. Peter’s Basilica
stops.imageCaption: Glowing white Carrara marble masterpiece bathed in soft golden Vatican basilica light depicting a serene, timelessly young Mother gently cradling her Son with boundless tenderness and open left palm.
stops.whatYouCanSeeToday: Inside the very first chapel on the right as you enter **St. Peter’s Basilica**, millions stand silently moved before Michelangelo’s *Pietà*—the ONLY artwork the great master ever proudly signed with his own name across Mary’s sash!
stops.didYouKnowHighlight: In 1814, right after being freed from five long years of Napoleon’s harsh imprisonment, Pope Pius VII gratefully extended **September 15 (Our Lady of Sorrows)** to the entire universal Church—and today **Slovakia** honors Our Lady of Sorrows as its beloved national Patroness!
stops.saintQuote: No tear shed in love is ever wasted in the eyes of God.

hiddenArtifacts.foundTitle: Tender Grief Carved in Marble: Michelangelo’s Pietà
hiddenArtifacts.storyUnlocked: When a twenty-four-year-old Florentine sculptor named **Michelangelo Buonarroti** picked up his chisel in 1498 to carve a single gleaming block of white Carrara marble for Rome, he poured the entire soul of **Our Lady of Sorrows** into the ***Pietà***! Look closely at Mary’s left hand: she isn’t clenching her fist in bitterness or anger—she gently opens her palm outward in serene, heartbreaking offering, inviting the whole watching world to draw close and never walk alone through grief.
